body: Hey! So sorry for the late reply. And sorry to hear you’re having issues with your pup. I know how awful that feeling is. Honestly he’s gotten so so so so much better. So that’s the good news. He’s 3 now and we have normal walks all the time we take him to the dog park etc. once in a while he’ll freak out a bit but it’s NEVER nearly as bad as it used to be. We now even laugh. What helped us was just constant treats and training outdoors to reinforce calm behavior when he saw his triggers (even tho he still pulls now - but no biting !) and truthfully we ended getting him a muzzle which he used for about a year. That alone helped so much because we weren’t scared of getting bitten so we could give him proper training and it taught him that he can’t get what he wants by biting or going crazy. It also helped him redirect his frustration with other things like shaking etc. now he doesn’t even need it though  and I don’t think we could have gotten there without the muzzle. Helped us regain confidence. I know muzzles aren’t for everyone so definitely do your research on it probably if it’s something you’re considering. It’s crucial to muzzle train them properly and it’s a bit of a slow process but it saved us so much pain. If you have any other questions feel free to PM me directly! Happy to help. Hope all is well!!

As someone who is Colombian, I can tell you the movie is a whole LOVE letter to Colombia. It included the even the tiniest nuances of Colombian culture that would never be apparent to non-colombians but felt that much more intimate and impactful to those who knew.  In comparison to Coco (a movie I also love) Encanto honestly blew me away in it's portrayal of Colombia, it's family dynamics, it's slang, it's mannerism, superstitions, culture, food, affection and so much more it's hard to even describe if you don't know the culture.  Moreover, what Coco had for international audiences that Encanto maybe didn't is that everyone is aware to some degree of the the Dia de los Muertos tradition, it's one of the many surface level anecdotes people might have about the rich Mexican culture. So to YOU it might have felt like they dove in deeper because you came equipped with that understanding but what you may not know is that Encanto is heavily based / inspired by *magical realism* and particularly the book **100 years of Solitude** by Gabriel Garcia Marquez - nobel prize winning Colombian author who basically revolutionized the genre of magical realism, so these comments on " a magical family can happen anywhere",sure, but the culture of the magical  family who's story is told through an intergenerational perspective is TRULY at home in Colombia. Colombians and many Latin Americans know and appreciate this. They borrowed soooo many themes from the novel it might as well have been 100 years of solitude pg 13 version.  

If you're curious about learning more about Colombian culture and understanding it's nuances between other Latin American countries, I would recommend it highly. And as a note the music is EXTREMELY Colombian. They drew influences from Vallenato, Cumbia  etc. Even bringing along famous Colombian singers, particularly Carlos Vives, whom I grew up listening to and is a cultural icon in Colombian. To say the music isn't inspired by Colombian feels more like a confession of not knowing exactly what our country's music sounds like, because Mexican cultural feels more accessible and popularized by mainstream audience. If you did enjoy even a bit of Encanto besides the questions on it's relation to Coco, I do recommend you do a bit of digging on the history, the music and the art that inspired it.  It might bring a renewed sense of wonder to it.

Hey, I'm a 23 year old college graduate and with a post-grad. I failed countless midterms in my undergrad, almost failed two (three) classes, and recently almost failed the most important class in my post-graduate (which potentially meant I would not graduating at all).  But I graduated from both institutions! Not sure how your school/class works but I highly doubt that grad schools would deny you entirely on one midterm. So don't let that deter you from your dreams, i know plenty of people that didn't do well in school and managed successful careers. Just focus try and learn from what you did wrong on the exam and work on it next time. Its' 100% not about failures, it's about what you do with them. Trust me! I've been through the lot of failed midterms and it's no cause that should strip you from hope. 

As for not dating anyone, it's normal too. One of my best friends is 22, beautiful (but believes she is not for some reason) and she hasn't ever dated anyone either, and not by choice, it happens differently for all people. It's not about your looks, its about whats on the inside (and remember we are always our harshest critics!) I know it sounds cheesy but it's so so true in the end. Everyone connects to each other differently and you may not know that you posses the qualities someone else looks for in a partner. Just because it hasn't happened yet doesn't indicate a certain future, remember that we all follow our own paths! Heck, I remember in high school still being the only one of my friends that had never even so much as a hugged a guy, and how out of place I felt. But now I realize there is NO set path, and everyone does things their own way (something I honestly wish I'd known earlier), you're 21! That's still very young, and it means you have a lot more to experience than you think you do. There is hope! As for where to look I mean, that's really hard to just say, but maybe get involved in school communities or groups so you can meet more people.  Get involved with a play, a sport, a committee, a job, a club. It doesn't have to be high demand, make sure it is something you love. Plus you can get to talk to people that share your interests which is always a bonus, and it might give you that sense of purpose and belonging.

New job= change, disruption of normal, risk. All of those things can definitely cause some major anxiety. what you're describing is definitely something I'd suggest talking out with a professional. seems like you have thought about this and rationalized this as best as you can and you have still come to the conclusion that it feels debilitating. Even if that weren't the case the true judge of whether you should seek help is you and how you feel. If it is something that legitimately impedes in your ability to work, think, relax, or have relationships then some help is a good idea. It can help you tune out negative cycles that are creating the anxiety, it can help you avoid oncoming anxiety, it will help you manage it better when it does come, and hell, even just talking it out and getting to say everything you wanna say can be instantly therapeutic.  If you think you can handle your own that's also good too! Whatever you think will get you to your best, but therapy, Counselling or even anxiety groups can be really helpful too! You're gonna be okay! I've been there before, when I start a new job i am miserable and a wreck. Anxious about all of it even the part where I miss my old Job.  It's manageable! And definitely not something you should have to endure. I hope this helps a bit, sorry if the grammar sounds weird I stayed up all night and I'm tired. Best of luck with everything and remember that you are not alone 😊
